State of Wisconsin Partial Veto Referendum - QUESTION 1
contests.question: QUESTION 1: “Partial veto. Shall section 10 (1) (c) of article V of the constitution be amended to prohibit the governor, in exercising his or her partial veto authority, from creating or increasing or authorizing the creation or increase of any tax or fee?”

contests.contest: State of Wisconsin Freedom to Gather in Places of Worship During an Emergency Referendum - QUESTION 2
contests.question: QUESTION 2: "Freedom to gather in places of worship during an emergency. Shall section 18 of article I of the constitution, which deals with religious liberty, be amended to prohibit the state or a political subdivision of the state from ordering the closure of, or forbidding gatherings in, places of worship in response to a state of emergency, including a public health emergency?"

contests.contest: State of Wisconsin Governmental Entity Discrimination Prohibited Referendum - QUESTION 3
contests.question: QUESTION 3: "Governmental entity discrimination prohibited. Shall section 27 of article I of the constitution be created to prohibit governmental entities in the state from discriminating against, or granting preferential treatment to, any individual or group on the basis of race, sex, color, ethnicity, or national origin in public employment, public education, public contracting, or public administration?"

contests.contest: Lafayette County Capital Expenditures Referendum - QUESTION 1
contests.question:
QUESTION 1: “Should the Lafayette County Board of Supervisors authorize and approve the County

incurring capital expenditures associated with the construction of a new nursing home, borrowing

funds to support the capital expenditures and levying a property tax to support the debt service

payments that will be above the allowable levy limit established in state law?”

contests.contest: Lafayette County Levy Increase Referendum - QUESTION 2
contests.question:
QUESTION 2: “Under state law, the increase in the levy of the County of Lafayette for the tax to be

imposed for the next fiscal year, 2027, is limited to 1.088%, which results in an estimated levy of

$10,087,262. Shall the County of Lafayette be allowed to exceed this limit and increase the levy for

the next fiscal year, 2027, for the purpose of paying a portion of the cost to operate and maintain

Lafayette Manor, by an estimated total of 4.957% which results in a levy of $10,587,262, and include

the increase of $500,000 for fiscal years 2028 through 2031?”

contests.contest: City of Hudson Fire Department Staffing Referendum
contests.question: Under state law, the increase in the levy of the City of Hudson for the tax to be imposed for the next fiscal year, 2027, is limited to 0.872%, which results in a levy of $13,335,657. Shall the City of Hudson be allowed to exceed this limit and increase the levy for the next fiscal year, 2027, for the purpose of improving emergency services with 9 additional full-time fire staff and ongoing Hudson Fire Department expenses, by a total of 9.698%, which results in a levy of $14,628,943 and on ongoing basis, include the increase of $1,293,285.68 for each fiscal year going forward?

contests.contest: City of Muskego Levy Increase Referendum
contests.question: Under state law, the increase in the levy of the City of Muskego for the tax to be imposed for the next fiscal year, 2027, is limited to 1.593%, which results in a levy of $14,732,877.00. Shall the City of Muskego be allowed to exceed this limit and increase the levy for the next fiscal year, 2027, for the purpose of improving public safety services in the City of Muskego, which, are the City’s Police, Fire, EMS, Rescue, and Public Works services, including staffing and support for those services, by a total of 40.047%, which results in a levy of $20,632,877.00, and on an ongoing basis, include the increase of $5,900,000.00 for each fiscal year going forward?

contests.question: Under state law, the increase in the levy of the City of New Berlin for the tax to be imposed for the next fiscal year, 2027, is limited to 0.762%, which results in a levy of $38,484,163. contests.contest: City of Plymouth Levy Increase Referendum

Shall the City of Plymouth be allowed to  exceed this limit and increase the levy for the next fiscal year, 2027, for the purpose of funding three additional police officers and related equipment and wage adjustments in the Police Department, by a total of 10.399%, which results in a levy of $6,369,712 and on an ongoing basis, include the increase of $600,000 for each fiscal year going forward?
